#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ -r /etc/default/labwc-desktop ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  . /etc/default/labwc-desktop
fi

systemctl_cmd=$(command -v systemctl 2>/dev/null || true)
activation_environment_names='LABWC_SESSION_OWNER DESKTOP_SESSION XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_TYPE XDG_RUNTIME_DIR WAYLAND_DISPLAY DISPLAY SWAYSOCK DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS XDG_CONFIG_DIRS XDG_DATA_DIRS MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT QT_QPA_PLATFORM QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION GDK_BACKEND SDL_VIDEODRIVER CLUTTER_BACKEND XCURSOR_THEME XCURSOR_SIZE GTK_THEME GTK_A11Y NO_AT_BRIDGE WLR_RENDERER GSK_RENDERER GDK_DISABLE WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS _JAVA_AWT_WM_NONREPARENTING'

if [ "${LABWC_SESSION_OWNER:-}" != desktop ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ]; then
  printf 'fatal: Labwc did not provide WAYLAND_DISPLAY to autostart\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

[ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ] || {
  printf 'fatal: systemctl is required to activate the Labwc user session\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

desktop_enabled() {
  case "${1:-true}" in
    true|yes|1|on) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

sync_user_activation_environment() {
  sync_attempt=1
  while [ "$sync_attempt" -le 5 ]; do
    sync_ok=true

    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user import-environment $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user set-environment LABWC_SESSION_OWNER=desktop >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false

    if command -v dbus-update-activation-environment >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    else
      sync_ok=false
    fi

    [ "$sync_ok" = true ] && return 0
    sleep 1
    sync_attempt=$((sync_attempt + 1))
  done

  printf 'fatal: unable to import the Labwc Wayland environment into the user manager\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

start_session_target() {
  "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-session.target >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    printf 'fatal: unable to activate the Labwc user session target\n' >&2
    exit 1
  }
}

start_waybar_if_enabled() {
  if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_WAYBAR:-true}" &&
     [ -r "$HOME/.config/waybar/config" ] &&
     [ -r "$HOME/.config/waybar/style.css" ]
  then
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start waybar.service >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
      printf 'warning: unable to request Waybar startup from the user manager\n' >&2
  fi
}

start_health_notifier_if_enabled() {
  if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_MAKO:-true}" &&
     [ -r "$HOME/.config/mako/config" ]
  then
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.path >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

sync_user_activation_environment
start_session_target
start_waybar_if_enabled
start_health_notifier_if_enabled

profile managed-labwc-greeter-session /usr/local/bin/labwc-greeter-session flags=(attach_disconnected) {
  #include <abstractions/managed-wrapper-desktop>

  /usr/local/bin/labwc-greeter-session rix,
  /usr/bin/{cat,chmod,id,install,mktemp,rm,sleep} rix,
  /usr/bin/udevadm pux,
  /usr/bin/{gtkgreet,labwc} pux,
  /usr/local/bin/labwc-greeter-output rPx -> managed-labwc-greeter-output,
  /usr/local/bin/labwc-greeter-power rPx -> managed-labwc-greeter-power,
  /usr/local/sbin/greetd-power-action rPx -> managed-greetd-power-action,
  signal (send) peer=managed-labwc-greeter-output,
  signal (send) peer=managed-labwc-greeter-power,
  /etc/greetd/gtkgreet.css r,
  /etc/xdg/labwc/ r,
  /etc/xdg/labwc/** r,
  /run/user/[0-9]*/labwc-greeter.*/ rw,
  /run/user/[0-9]*/labwc-greeter.*/** rwkl,
  /tmp/labwc-greeter.*/ rw,
  /tmp/labwc-greeter.*/** rwkl,

  include if exists <local/usr.local.bin.labwc-greeter-session>
}

profile managed-labwc-session /usr/local/bin/labwc-session flags=(attach_disconnected) {
  #include <abstractions/managed-wrapper-desktop>

  /usr/local/bin/labwc-session rix,
  /usr/bin/{flock,stat} rix,
  /usr/bin/{dbus-update-activation-environment,systemctl} pux,
  /usr/bin/labwc pux,
  # The compositor wrapper retains the one session lock while Labwc runs and
  # closes its descriptor in the compositor child.
  owner @{HOME}/ r,
  owner @{HOME}/.profile r,
  owner @{HOME}/.profile.d/ r,
  owner @{HOME}/.profile.d/* r,
  owner /run/user/[0-9]*/labwc-session.lock rwk,
  /etc/xdg/labwc/ r,
  /etc/xdg/labwc/** r,

  include if exists <local/usr.local.bin.labwc-session>
}

profile managed-labwc-terminal /usr/local/bin/labwc-terminal flags=(attach_disconnected) {
  #include <abstractions/managed-wrapper-desktop>

  /usr/local/bin/labwc-terminal rix,
  /usr/bin/{foot,kitty,x-terminal-emulator} pux,

  include if exists <local/usr.local.bin.labwc-terminal>

set -eu
account_user=$1
default_groups=$2

getent passwd "$account_user" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  printf "fatal: primary account is missing from target passwd: %s\n" "$account_user" >&2
  exit 1
}
account_uid=$(id -u "$account_user")
account_gid=$(id -g "$account_user")
case "$account_uid:$account_gid" in
  0:*|65534:*|*:65534)
    printf "fatal: refusing unsafe primary account uid/gid mapping for %s: %s:%s\n" \
      "$account_user" "$account_uid" "$account_gid" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

getent group devops >/dev/null 2>&1 || groupadd --system devops
required_groups="${default_groups} devops"
current_groups=$(id -nG "$account_user")
missing_groups=

for group_name in $required_groups; do
  case "$group_name" in
    [abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_]*)
      ;;
    *)
      printf "fatal: invalid primary account group name: %s\n" "$group_name" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
  case "$group_name" in
    *[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-]*)
      printf "fatal: invalid primary account group name: %s\n" "$group_name" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
  getent group "$group_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    printf "fatal: required primary account group is missing: %s\n" "$group_name" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  case " $current_groups " in
    *" $group_name "*) ;;
    *) missing_groups="${missing_groups:+$missing_groups,}$group_name" ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$missing_groups" ]; then
  usermod -a -G "$missing_groups" -- "$account_user"
  current_groups=$(id -nG "$account_user")
fi

for group_name in $required_groups; do
  case " $current_groups " in
    *" $group_name "*) ;;
    *)
      printf "fatal: primary account group assignment failed for %s: missing %s\n" \
        "$account_user" "$group_name" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

for root_owned_path in / /etc /usr /usr/bin /etc/passwd /etc/group /etc/sudo.conf; do
  [ -e "$root_owned_path" ] || {
    printf "fatal: required root-owned target path is missing: %s\n" "$root_owned_path" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  root_owned_ids=$(stat -c "%u:%g" "$root_owned_path")
  [ "$root_owned_ids" = 0:0 ] || {
    printf "fatal: target path must be owned by root:root, found %s: %s\n" \
      "$root_owned_ids" "$root_owned_path" >&2
    exit 1
  }
done

sudo_metadata=$(stat -c "%u:%g:%a" /usr/bin/sudo)
case "$sudo_metadata" in
  0:0:[4567][0-7][0-7][0-7])
    ;;
  *)
    printf "fatal: /usr/bin/sudo must be root-owned with setuid enabled, found %s\n" \
      "$sudo_metadata" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

printf "account_access user=%s uid=%s gid=%s groups=%s\n" \
  "$account_user" "$account_uid" "$account_gid" "$current_groups"
' sh "$ACCOUNT_USERNAME" "$ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_GROUPS"

## Summary

Your **bwrap hypothesis is technically reasonable**, because a single-ID user namespace makes root-owned files appear as UID/GID `65534`, which resolves to `nobody:nogroup`.

However, repository inspection shows:

- **gtkgreet is not launched through bwrap or `unshare`.** It runs directly as:
  `greetd → labwc-greeter-session → labwc → gtkgreet`  
  [config.toml.tmpl](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/etc/greetd/config.toml.tmpl#L1)  
  [labwc-greeter-session.tmpl](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-greeter-session.tmpl#L98)

- **The real Labwc session is not launched through bwrap.** Greetd executes `/usr/local/bin/labwc-session`, which directly executes `/usr/bin/labwc`.  
  [labwc.desktop](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/share/wayland-sessions/labwc.desktop#L1)  
  [labwc-session.tmpl](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-session.tmpl#L89)

- AppArmor permits these executables but does **not** create a user namespace. There is no `bwrap`, `unshare`, `PrivateUsers=`, `RootDirectory=`, or `RootImage=` in the greeter/session chain.

- Bubblewrap is used only for explicitly sandboxed applications:
  - `pure-privacy` managed application mode.
  - Persistent Tutanota sandbox.
  - Managed qBittorrent sandbox.  
  [labwc-managed-app](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-managed-app#L1479)  
  [labwc-managed-app](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-managed-app#L1786)  
  [labwc-qbittorrent](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-qbittorrent#L463)

### Should `labwc-session.target` be a system target?

**No. It should remain a user target.**

The services attached to it require:

- The authenticated user identity and home directory.
- `%h`.
- The user D-Bus.
- `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.
- The user’s Wayland socket.
- The environment exported by the running compositor.
- Automatic shutdown when that user’s Labwc session exits.

Turning it into a system target would either run desktop components as root or require manually duplicating the user identity, runtime-directory, D-Bus and Wayland environment handling. That would be less secure and substantially less reliable.

[labwc-session.target](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/etc/skel/.config/systemd/user/labwc-session.target#L1) is correctly a per-user lifecycle boundary. The system-level components should remain `greetd.service`, `systemd-logind.service`, `seatd.service`, and `firstboot.service`.

## Tests

Repository searches confirmed:

- No namespace creation in:
  - `labwc-greeter-session`
  - `labwc-session`
  - `labwc-autostart`
  - `labwc-terminal`
  - `labwc-session.target`
- No `PrivateUsers=` in the greeter or normal desktop user services.
- Bubblewrap call sites are limited to the managed application sandbox paths listed above.
- Late installation validates `/`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/usr/bin`, `/etc/passwd`, and `/etc/group` as numeric `0:0` before first boot.  
  [account.sh](d-i/forky/scripts/late/account.sh#L319)

## Risks/Follow-ups

If `nobody:nogroup` appeared inside a **normal Foot or Kitty terminal**, it was not caused by the repository’s managed-application bwrap logic.

The remaining plausible namespace causes are:

1. An external/vendor `greetd.service` or `user@.service` namespace setting not represented in this repository.
2. The process was actually opened from one of the explicitly sandboxed applications.
3. A transient first-boot process/session namespace inherited outside the visible wrapper chain.
4. Less likely: broken NSS resolution—but that normally displays numeric IDs rather than converting numeric `0` to `65534`.

## Next steps

The correct next hardening is **not** converting `labwc-session.target` into a system service. It is adding a fail-fast namespace check to both session wrappers:

```sh
[ "$(readlink /proc/self/ns/user)" = "$(readlink /proc/1/ns/user)" ]
```

If the namespace differs, the wrapper should log `/proc/self/uid_map` and refuse to start Labwc. That would conclusively detect the condition that turns host UID `0` into `65534` before the user enters a broken desktop session.

activation_environment_names='LABWC_SESSION_OWNER DESKTOP_SESSION XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_TYPE XDG_RUNTIME_DIR WAYLAND_DISPLAY DISPLAY SWAYSOCK DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS XDG_CONFIG_DIRS XDG_DATA_DIRS MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT QT_QPA_PLATFORM QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION GDK_BACKEND SDL_VIDEODRIVER CLUTTER_BACKEND XCURSOR_THEME XCURSOR_SIZE GTK_THEME GTK_A11Y NO_AT_BRIDGE WLR_RENDERER GSK_RENDERER GDK_DISABLE WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS _JAVA_AWT_WM_NONREPARENTING'

if [ "${LABWC_SESSION_OWNER:-}" != desktop ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ]; then
  printf 'fatal: Labwc did not provide WAYLAND_DISPLAY to autostart\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

[ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ] || {
  printf 'fatal: systemctl is required to activate the Labwc user session\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

desktop_enabled() {
  case "${1:-true}" in
    true|yes|1|on) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

sync_user_activation_environment() {
  sync_attempt=1
  while [ "$sync_attempt" -le 5 ]; do
    sync_ok=true

    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user import-environment $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user set-environment LABWC_SESSION_OWNER=desktop >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false

    if command -v dbus-update-activation-environment >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    else
      sync_ok=false
    fi

    [ "$sync_ok" = true ] && return 0
    sleep 1
    sync_attempt=$((sync_attempt + 1))
  done

  printf 'fatal: unable to import the Labwc Wayland environment into the user manager\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

start_session_target() {
  "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-session.target >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    printf 'fatal: unable to activate the Labwc user session target\n' >&2
    exit 1
  }
}

     [ -r "$HOME/.config/waybar/config" ] &&
     [ -r "$HOME/.config/waybar/style.css" ]
  then
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start waybar.service >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
      printf 'warning: unable to request Waybar startup from the user manager\n' >&2
  fi

    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

sync_user_activation_environment
start_session_target

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ -r /etc/default/labwc-desktop ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  . /etc/default/labwc-desktop
fi

systemctl_cmd=$(command -v systemctl 2>/dev/null || true)
HYPRPOLKITAGENT_PATH=
activation_environment_names='LABWC_SESSION_OWNER DESKTOP_SESSION XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP XDG_SESSION_TYPE XDG_RUNTIME_DIR WAYLAND_DISPLAY DISPLAY SWAYSOCK DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS XDG_CONFIG_DIRS XDG_DATA_DIRS MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT QT_QPA_PLATFORM QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION GDK_BACKEND SDL_VIDEODRIVER CLUTTER_BACKEND XCURSOR_THEME XCURSOR_SIZE GTK_THEME GTK_A11Y NO_AT_BRIDGE WLR_RENDERER GSK_RENDERER GDK_DISABLE WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS _JAVA_AWT_WM_NONREPARENTING'

if [ "${LABWC_SESSION_OWNER:-}" != desktop ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ]; then
  printf 'fatal: Labwc did not provide WAYLAND_DISPLAY to autostart\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

[ -x /usr/bin/flock ] || {
  printf 'fatal: /usr/bin/flock is required to serialize Labwc autostart\n' >&2
  exit 1
}
exec 9>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/labwc-autostart.lock"
/usr/bin/flock -w 10 9 || exit 0

desktop_enabled() {
  case "${1:-true}" in
    true|yes|1|on) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

require_non_negative_integer() {
  value_name=$1
  value=$2

  case "$value" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*)
      printf 'fatal: %s must be a non-negative integer, got: %s\n' "$value_name" "$value" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
}

require_idle_timeout_order() {
  lock_seconds=$1
  dpms_seconds=$2
  suspend_seconds=$3

  if [ "$dpms_seconds" -le "$lock_seconds" ]; then
    printf 'fatal: LABWC_IDLE_DPMS_SECONDS (%s) must be greater than LABWC_IDLE_LOCK_SECONDS (%s) so the lock screen appears before the outputs sleep\n' \
      "$dpms_seconds" \
      "$lock_seconds" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if [ "$suspend_seconds" -gt 0 ] &&
     [ "$suspend_seconds" -le "$dpms_seconds" ]; then
    printf 'fatal: LABWC_IDLE_SUSPEND_SECONDS (%s) must be greater than LABWC_IDLE_DPMS_SECONDS (%s) when suspend is enabled\n' \
      "$suspend_seconds" \
      "$dpms_seconds" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

start_background() {
  command_name=$1
  shift

  command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  (
    exec 9>&- 2>/dev/null || true
    exec "$command_name" "$@"
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
}

start_background_once() {
  lock_name=$1
  command_name=$2
  shift 2

  case "$lock_name" in
    ''|*[!ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789._-]*)
      printf 'fatal: invalid Labwc component lock name: %s\n' "$lock_name" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  lock_path="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/labwc-${lock_name}.lock"
  (
    exec 9>&- 2>/dev/null || true
    # Keep the lock in flock's parent process so AppArmor profile transitions
    # never inherit the lock descriptor into the managed command or descendants.
    exec /usr/bin/flock --nonblock --close "$lock_path" "$command_name" "$@"
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
}

find_first_executable() {
  for candidate_path in "$@"; do
    [ -x "$candidate_path" ] || continue
    printf '%s\n' "$candidate_path"
    return 0
  done
  return 1
}

refresh_outputs_now() {
  command -v labwc-output-refresh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  labwc-output-refresh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

wayland_output_ready() {
  [ -x /usr/bin/wlr-randr ] || return 1
  output_snapshot=$(
    /usr/bin/timeout 2 /usr/bin/wlr-randr 2>/dev/null || true
  )
  [ -n "$output_snapshot" ]
}

wait_for_wayland_output() {
  output_attempt=1
  while [ "$output_attempt" -le 100 ]; do
    wayland_output_ready && return 0
    /usr/bin/sleep 0.1
    output_attempt=$((output_attempt + 1))
  done

  printf 'fatal: Labwc did not expose a usable Wayland output within 10 seconds\n' >&2
  return 1
}

waybar_compatible_desktop() {
  waybar_desktop=${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-labwc:wlroots}
  case ":$waybar_desktop:" in
    *:Unity:*) ;;
    *) waybar_desktop="Unity:${waybar_desktop}" ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$waybar_desktop"
}

start_waybar() {
  if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ]; then
    if "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start waybar.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      waybar_start_attempt=1
      while [ "$waybar_start_attempt" -le 20 ]; do
        if "$systemctl_cmd" --user --quiet is-active waybar.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          return 0
        fi
        sleep 0.1
        waybar_start_attempt=$((waybar_start_attempt + 1))
      done
    fi
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user stop waybar.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  waybar_desktop=$(waybar_compatible_desktop)
  start_background_once \
    waybar \
    /usr/bin/env \
    "XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=${waybar_desktop}" \
    waybar \
    -c "$HOME/.config/waybar/config" \
    -s "$HOME/.config/waybar/style.css"
}

start_mako() {
  if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ] &&
     "$systemctl_cmd" --user start mako.service >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
     "$systemctl_cmd" --user --quiet is-active mako.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi
  start_background_once mako mako -c "$HOME/.config/mako/config"
}

start_polkit_agent() {
  if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ] &&
     "$systemctl_cmd" --user start hyprpolkitagent.service >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
     "$systemctl_cmd" --user --quiet is-active hyprpolkitagent.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -z "$HYPRPOLKITAGENT_PATH" ]; then
    HYPRPOLKITAGENT_PATH=$(find_first_executable \
      /usr/libexec/hyprpolkitagent \
      /usr/lib/hyprpolkitagent \
      /usr/lib64/hyprpolkitagent 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  [ -n "$HYPRPOLKITAGENT_PATH" ] || return 0
  start_background_once \
    polkit-agent \
    /usr/bin/env \
    QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland \
    QT_NO_XDG_DESKTOP_PORTAL=1 \
    "$HYPRPOLKITAGENT_PATH"
}

start_health_notifier() {
  if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ]; then
    health_watch_started=false
    if "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.path >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      health_watch_started=true
    fi
    if "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.timer >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      health_watch_started=true
    fi
    if [ "$health_watch_started" = true ]; then
      "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-health-notify.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  start_background labwc-health-notify
}

start_labwc_session_target() {
  if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ]; then
    "$systemctl_cmd" --user --no-block start labwc-session.target >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
      printf 'fatal: unable to activate the Labwc user session target\n' >&2
      return 1
    }

    session_target_attempt=1
    while [ "$session_target_attempt" -le 50 ]; do
      if "$systemctl_cmd" --user --quiet is-active labwc-session.target >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
      fi
      sleep 0.1
      session_target_attempt=$((session_target_attempt + 1))
    done

    printf 'fatal: Labwc user session target did not become active within 5 seconds\n' >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

sync_user_activation_environment() {
  sync_attempt=1
  while [ "$sync_attempt" -le 5 ]; do
    sync_ok=true
    if [ -n "$systemctl_cmd" ]; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      "$systemctl_cmd" --user import-environment $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
      "$systemctl_cmd" --user set-environment LABWC_SESSION_OWNER=desktop >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    else
      sync_ok=false
    fi

    if command -v dbus-update-activation-environment >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd $activation_environment_names >/dev/null 2>&1 || sync_ok=false
    else
      sync_ok=false
    fi

    [ "$sync_ok" = true ] && return 0
    sleep 1
    sync_attempt=$((sync_attempt + 1))
  done

  printf 'fatal: unable to import the Labwc Wayland environment into the user manager\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "--delayed-waybar" ]; then
  shift
  waybar_delay=${1:-0}
  require_non_negative_integer "Waybar delay" "$waybar_delay"
  sleep "$waybar_delay"
  start_waybar
  exit 0
fi

sync_user_activation_environment

wallpaper_path=${LABWC_WALLPAPER_PATH:-/usr/share/backgrounds/desktop/wallpaper-1920x1080.png}
saved_wallpaper_path=$(
  /usr/local/bin/labwc-wallpaper-save --current 2>/dev/null || true
)
if [ -n "$saved_wallpaper_path" ]; then
  wallpaper_path=$saved_wallpaper_path
fi
if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_SWAYBG:-true}" &&
   [ -r "$wallpaper_path" ]; then
  start_background_once swaybg swaybg -m fill -i "$wallpaper_path"
fi

refresh_outputs_now
start_background_once output-watch labwc-output-watch --skip-initial-refresh

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_KANSHI:-true}" && [ -r "$HOME/.config/kanshi/config" ]; then
  start_background_once kanshi kanshi
fi

wait_for_wayland_output
start_labwc_session_target

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_MAKO:-true}" && [ -r "$HOME/.config/mako/config" ]; then
  start_mako
  start_health_notifier
fi

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_POLKIT_AGENT:-true}"; then
  start_polkit_agent
fi

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_WAYBAR:-true}" && [ -r "$HOME/.config/waybar/config" ]; then
  waybar_delay=${LABWC_WAYBAR_START_DELAY_SECONDS:-2}
  require_non_negative_integer LABWC_WAYBAR_START_DELAY_SECONDS "$waybar_delay"
  if [ "$waybar_delay" -gt 0 ]; then
    start_background labwc-autostart --delayed-waybar "$waybar_delay"
  else
    start_waybar
  fi
fi

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_CRYSTAL_DOCK:-true}"; then
  start_background labwc-dock
fi

if desktop_enabled "${LABWC_ENABLE_SWAYIDLE:-true}"; then
  lock_seconds=${LABWC_IDLE_LOCK_SECONDS:-600}
  dpms_seconds=${LABWC_IDLE_DPMS_SECONDS:-1800}
  suspend_seconds=${LABWC_IDLE_SUSPEND_SECONDS:-0}
  require_non_negative_integer LABWC_IDLE_LOCK_SECONDS "$lock_seconds"
  require_non_negative_integer LABWC_IDLE_DPMS_SECONDS "$dpms_seconds"
  require_non_negative_integer LABWC_IDLE_SUSPEND_SECONDS "$suspend_seconds"
  require_idle_timeout_order "$lock_seconds" "$dpms_seconds" "$suspend_seconds"
  if [ "$suspend_seconds" -gt 0 ]; then
    start_background_once swayidle swayidle -w \
      timeout "$lock_seconds" labwc-lock \
      timeout "$dpms_seconds" 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-off' resume 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-on' \
      timeout "$suspend_seconds" 'systemctl suspend' \
      before-sleep labwc-lock \
      after-resume 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-on' \
      lock labwc-lock
  else
    start_background_once swayidle swayidle -w \
      timeout "$lock_seconds" labwc-lock \
      timeout "$dpms_seconds" 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-off' resume 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-on' \
      before-sleep labwc-lock \
      after-resume 'labwc-output-refresh --dpms-on' \
      lock labwc-lock
  fi
fi

exit 0

## Summary

You correctly identified `labwc-autostart` as the **critical unchecked boundary**.

It does **not create a bwrap namespace itself**, but before this change it blindly:

1. Trusted `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.
2. Trusted `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`.
3. Imported that environment into `systemd --user`.
4. Started `labwc-session.target`.

I have now hardened it so this happens **only when**:

- The process is a non-root authenticated user.
- `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is exactly `/run/user/<current UID>`.
- The runtime directory is owned by the current UID/GID.
- `/proc/self/uid_map` and `gid_map` describe the normal host identity namespace.
- The user D-Bus socket exists and is owned by the current UID/GID.
- `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` is forcibly reset to that verified socket instead of trusting an inherited value.

[labwc-autostart](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-autostart#L31)  
[validation invocation](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-autostart#L141)

The AppArmor profile now grants only the exact additional reads and commands needed for this validation:

[managed-desktop-wrappers](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/etc/apparmor.d/managed-desktop-wrappers#L122)

`labwc-session.target` should **remain a user target**. The problem was the unverified handoff to the user manager, not the fact that the target belongs to the user manager.

## Tests

- `sh -n labwc-autostart` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Normal host UID map simulation (`0 → 0`, full range) — accepted.
- Remapped UID map simulation (`1000 → 1000`, length 1) — rejected.
- The current Codex sandbox reproduces the exact reported behavior:
  - UID map: `1000 → 1000`, length 1.
  - `/`, `/etc`, and `/usr` appear as numeric `65534:65534`.
  - The new autostart guard rejects that context.
- `t/apparmor-wrapper-profiles-smoke.sh` — **27/27 passed**.
- Modified desktop checks:
  - Labwc autostart check — passed.
  - Session-target user-service binding — passed.
- The complete desktop smoke still has the same three unrelated user-owned failures in terminal styling, managed launchers, and zsh highlighting.

## Risks/Follow-ups

This proves that a remapped single-user namespace produces exactly the `nobody:nogroup` symptom and that `labwc-autostart` will no longer start or modify the user-manager environment in that state.

It does **not prove that autostart originally created the namespace**—it contains no bwrap or unshare invocation. If the guard triggers on the installed system, the namespace was created earlier in the parent chain. The new fatal message will now identify that condition instead of silently continuing.

## Next steps

On a fresh installation, if the namespace is normal, Labwc autostart proceeds normally. If it is remapped, it now fails immediately with:

```text
fatal: refusing Labwc autostart from a remapped user namespace UID map
```

That gives a definitive failure boundary instead of allowing a desktop where the host filesystem appears owned by `nobody:nogroup`.
